title: Explicit dual presentation for a section of a split node
statement: Let $A$ be any commutative ring, $a,b\in A$, $R=A[x,y]/(xy-ab)$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and $\epsilon:R\to A$ the augmentation $x\mapsto a$, $y\mapsto b$. Put $I=\ker\epsilon=(x-a,y-b)$ and $M=\operatorname{Hom}_R(I,R)$. Both $I$ and $M$ are finitely presented $R$-modules [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. There is a unique $R$-linear map $e:I\to R$ with $e(x-a)=-a$ and $e(y-b)=y$. If $\mathbf1:I\hookrightarrow R$ denotes inclusion, then the map $R^2\to M$, $(r,s)\mapsto r\mathbf1+se$, is surjective with kernel generated by $(a,x-a)$ and $(-y,y-b)$. The map $R\to M$, $r\mapsto r\mathbf1$, is injective, and the formula $r\mathbf1+se\mapsto\epsilon(s)$ gives an exact sequence $0\to R\to M\to A\to0$, where $R$ acts on $A$ through $\epsilon$. For every ring map $A\to A'$, with $R'=A'[x,y]/(xy-a'b')$ and $I'=\ker(R'\to A')$, the canonical maps $A'\otimes_A I\to I'$ and $A'\otimes_A M\to\operatorname{Hom}_{R'}(I',R')$ are isomorphisms carrying $\mathbf1,e$ and the displayed exact sequence to their primed counterparts. In addition, for every flat $R$-algebra $C$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], the canonical maps $C\otimes_R I\to IC$ and $C\otimes_R M\to\operatorname{Hom}_C(IC,C)$ are isomorphisms carrying the same generators to their induced homomorphisms, and $0\to C\to C\otimes_R M\to C/IC\to0$ is exact. Tensor products use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Knudsen, A Closer Look at the Stacks of Stable Pointed Curves, Section 3, Proposition 3.1 (matrix-factorization presentation) and Section 4, Main Lemma. Agent split-hyperbola coordinate version; arbitrary coefficient rings follow by the same finite polynomial presentation, rather than the source's Noetherian completion argument. Local PDF WANTED; primary author text read online.

proof.text: Write $B=A[X,Y]=A[u,v]$, where $u=X-a$, $v=Y-b$, and $f=XY-ab=Yu+av=uv+bu+av$. Translation and its inverse define the equality of polynomial rings by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Evaluation at $u=v=0$ has kernel $(u,v)$: subtract the constant term of each monomial to obtain a multiple of $u$ or $v$. Since $f$ evaluates to zero, this descends to $I=(u,v)\subset R=B/(f)$ and $R/I=A$. We use $u,v,X,Y$ also for their residue classes.

source.place: Knudsen, Section 3, matrix-factorization calculation preceding Proposition 3.1, adapted to the split equation; direct polynomial argument by O4 (local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: Multiplication by $u$ is injective in $B=A[v][u]$, and multiplication by $v$ is injective in $A[v]$, by shifting coefficients. Multiplication by $f$ is injective in $B$: for a nonzero finite polynomial $h$, choose its largest monomial in graded lexicographic order; the largest monomial of $fh$ is $XY$ times that monomial, with exactly its nonzero coefficient. Thus $fh\ne0$, even when $A$ has zero divisors. If $A$ is the zero ring all assertions are immediate. No cancellation in $R$ is asserted here.

source.place: Knudsen, Section 3, matrix-factorization calculation preceding Proposition 3.1, adapted to the split equation; direct polynomial argument by O4 (local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: For $p,q\in B$ with $up+vq=0$, set $u=0$ to get $v q(0,v)=0$, hence $q(0,v)=0$ and $q=ut$ for some $t\in B$. Cancelling $u$ gives $p=-vt$. Thus the polynomial relations of $(u,v)$ are exactly the multiples of $(-v,u)$. If $(p,q)\in R^2$ has $up+vq=0$, lift it to $B^2$ and write $u\widetilde p+v\widetilde q=fh$. Subtract $h(Y,a)$ and apply the preceding calculation. Therefore $\ker(R^2\xrightarrow{(u,v)}I)$ is generated by $(Y,a)$ and $(-v,u)$. In particular, with $K$ the matrix with first row $(Y,-v)$ and second row $(a,u)$, the sequence $R^2\xrightarrow K R^2\to I\to0$ is exact.

source.place: Knudsen, Section 3, matrix-factorization calculation preceding Proposition 3.1, adapted to the split equation; direct polynomial argument by O4 (local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: Over $B$, put $Q=K^{\mathsf t}$, whose rows are $(Y,a)$ and $(-v,u)$, and let $T$ have rows $(u,-a)$ and $(v,Y)$. Direct multiplication gives $QT=TQ=f\,\mathrm{id}$. The reductions modulo $f$ satisfy $\ker Q=\operatorname{im}T$: if $Qz=0$ in $R^2$, choose lifts with $Q\widetilde z=fw$; multiplying by $T$ and cancelling $f$ coordinatewise gives $\widetilde z=Tw$. Conversely $QT=0$ in $R$. Exchanging $Q,T$ gives $\ker T=\operatorname{im}Q$. These are explicit two-vector lifting calculations; no general matrix-factorization theorem is used.

source.place: Knudsen, Section 3, matrix-factorization calculation preceding Proposition 3.1, adapted to the split equation; direct polynomial argument by O4 (local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: An $R$-linear homomorphism $I\to R$ is determined by its values on $u,v$. By the presentation in step 3, a pair of values $(h,k)$ defines such a map precisely when $Yh+ak=0$ and $-vh+uk=0$, namely when $(h,k)\in\ker Q$. Step 4 identifies this kernel with the image of $T$. Its first column $(u,v)$ gives the inclusion $\mathbf1$, and its second column $(-a,Y)$ gives the unique map $e$ with $e(u)=-a$, $e(v)=Y$. Thus $\Phi:R^2\to M$, $(r,s)\mapsto r\mathbf1+se$, is surjective. Its kernel is $\ker T=\operatorname{im}Q$, generated by $(a,u)$ and $(Y,-v)$, equivalently $(a,x-a)$ and $(-y,y-b)$.

source.place: Knudsen, Section 3, matrix-factorization calculation preceding Proposition 3.1, adapted to the split equation; direct polynomial argument by O4 (local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: The finite presentations $R^2\xrightarrow K R^2\to I\to0$ and $R^2\xrightarrow Q R^2\to M\to0$ show directly that both modules are finitely presented, by [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].

source.place: Knudsen, Section 3, matrix-factorization calculation preceding Proposition 3.1, adapted to the split equation; direct polynomial argument by O4 (local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: The inclusion-multiplier map $R\to M$ is injective. Indeed, if $r\mathbf1=0$, step 5 gives $(r,0)=Q(c,d)=(Yc+ad,-vc+ud)$. Apply the relation calculation of step 3 to $(d,-c)$, since $ud-vc=0$: there are $h,k\in R$ with $d=Yh-vk$ and $-c=ah+uk$. Substitution gives $r=Y(-ah-uk)+a(Yh-vk)=-(Yu+av)k=0$.

source.place: Knudsen, Section 3, matrix-factorization calculation preceding Proposition 3.1, adapted to the split equation; direct polynomial argument by O4 (local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: The rule $(r,s)\mapsto\epsilon(s)$ kills the two columns of $Q$, because their second coordinates are $-v$ and $u$. It therefore induces $\pi:M\to A$, which is surjective since $\pi(e)=1$. If $\epsilon(s)=0$, write $s=uh+vk$ using step 1. The relations of step 5 give $ue=-a\mathbf1$ and $ve=Y\mathbf1$, so $r\mathbf1+se=(r-ah+Yk)\mathbf1$. Conversely $\pi(r\mathbf1)=0$. Together with step 7 this proves the asserted short exact sequence. The action on the quotient is through $R/(u,v)=A$.

source.place: Knudsen, Section 3, matrix-factorization calculation preceding Proposition 3.1, adapted to the split equation; direct polynomial argument by O4 (local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: For an $S$-algebra $D$ and an $S$-module $V$, $D\otimes_S V^2\cong(D\otimes_S V)^2$ sends $d\otimes(v,w)$ to $(d\otimes v,d\otimes w)$; the inverse sends $(d\otimes v,d'\otimes w)$ to $d\otimes(v,0)+d'\otimes(0,w)$ and extends additively. Bilinearity verifies well-definedness and both composites. For $A\to A'$, the tensor universal property identifies $A'\otimes_A B$ with $A'[X,Y]$ via $c\otimes\sum d_{ij}X^iY^j\mapsto\sum c d'_{ij}X^iY^j$; its inverse sends $\sum c_{ij}X^iY^j$ to $\sum c_{ij}\otimes X^iY^j$. Applying right exactness to $B\xrightarrow f B\to R\to0$ identifies $A'\otimes_A R$ with $R'$. Tensoring the two finite presentations in steps 3 and 6, using [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], gives presentations by the entrywise primed matrices $K',Q'$. Steps 1--5 applied over the arbitrary ring $A'$ give exactly those presentations for $I'$ and $M'$. Hence the induced maps $A'\otimes_A I\to I'$ and $A'\otimes_A M\to M'$ are isomorphisms. They are the canonical maps: on generators they send $c\otimes u,c\otimes v$ to $cu',cv'$, and $c\otimes\mathbf1,c\otimes e$ to $c\mathbf1',ce'$; evaluating the latter on $u',v'$ gives the primed columns of $T$.

source.place: Tags 00CX (lemma-tensor-product) and 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact); direct comparison of the finite polynomial presentations.

proof.text: Under the comparisons of step 9, $c\otimes(r\mathbf1)$ maps to $cr'\mathbf1'$, and the quotient map sends $c\otimes(r\mathbf1+se)$ to $c\epsilon(s)'=\epsilon'(cs')$. The identification $A'\otimes_A A\cong A'$ is $c\otimes d\mapsto cd'$, with inverse $c\mapsto c\otimes1$; balancing gives $c\otimes d=cd'\otimes1$, so both composites are identities. Thus both arrows of the tensored sequence agree with the primed arrows. The primed sequence is exact by steps 7--8 applied over $A'$, proving the required sequence compatibility even for nonflat $A\to A'$. No preservation of injections by arbitrary tensoring is assumed.

source.place: Knudsen, Section 3, matrix-factorization calculation preceding Proposition 3.1, adapted to the split equation; direct polynomial argument by O4 (local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: Now let $C$ be flat over $R$. The bilinear flip $c\otimes n\mapsto n\otimes c$ defines an isomorphism $C\otimes_R N\cong N\otimes_R C$ with inverse the same flip; the formulas on pure tensors show it commutes with maps of $N$. Thus the cited injectivity formulation of flatness applies with $C$ in the left tensor factor as well. For any exact pair $U\xrightarrow g V\xrightarrow h W$, factor $g$ through $J=\operatorname{im}g=\ker h$ and $h$ through $L=\operatorname{im}h$. Tensor right exactness applied to $U\to J\to0$ and $J\to V\to L\to0$, together with injectivity of $C\otimes_R L\to C\otimes_R W$ from flatness, shows that $\ker(1\otimes h)=\operatorname{im}(1\otimes g)$. Apply this to the exact pairs $T,Q$ and $Q,T$ of step 4; their tensors are the same matrices over $C$, so $\ker Q_C=\operatorname{im}T_C$ and $\ker T_C=\operatorname{im}Q_C$. Flatness also makes $C\otimes_R I\to C$ injective; its image is the ideal generated by $u,v$, namely $IC$. Thus it identifies $C\otimes_R I$ with $IC$.

source.place: Tag 00HB (definition-flat), using its injectivity formulation in def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, and Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact); exactness established through the images explicitly.

proof.text: Tensoring the presentation of $I$ gives a presentation $C^2\xrightarrow{K_C}C^2\to IC\to0$. Therefore evaluation on $u,v$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_C(IC,C)$ with $\ker Q_C=\operatorname{im}T_C$. The tensor of the presentation of $M$ identifies $C\otimes_R M$ with $\operatorname{coker}Q_C$, which is isomorphic to that same image by $\ker T_C=\operatorname{im}Q_C$. This isomorphism is the canonical dual base-change map: $c\otimes\varphi$ acts by $di\mapsto cd\varphi(i)$ for $d\in C$, $i\in I$, and sends $\mathbf1,e$ to the maps with values $(u,v)$ and $(-a,Y)$. Finally, step 11 and flatness preserve the exact sequence of steps 7--8. The last term $C\otimes_R A$ is $C/IC$: $c\otimes\bar r\mapsto cr\bmod IC$, with inverse $\bar c\mapsto c\otimes1$. This proves the final exact sequence and its generator compatibility. Here $C\otimes_R R\cong C$ sends $c\otimes r$ to $cr$, with inverse $c\mapsto c\otimes1$; under it the first arrow sends $c$ to $c\mathbf1$, as claimed.
